title: Load Diffusion Plate and Cold Expanded Fastener Row at the Forward Cargo Frame Feet, Stations C24 to C31
abstract: Introduces a machined diffusion plate under the frame feet between stations C24 and C31 and takes the attachment row to the cold expanded standard, so that a repeat finding location is closed out rather than reset at every heavy check.

sections.reason: One operator has recorded twenty-three findings on nine aircraft over six years at the frame foot to cargo floor beam interface in the forward compartment, always on the left hand side and always within a metre of the same station. Two aircraft have had the same foot blended three times and are close to the limit of material that may be removed. Fleet-wide the same location accounts for one in three of all forward fuselage findings above twelve thousand cycles. The current answer is blend, inspect and repeat, which resets the interval without changing the detail that produced the crack.
sections.description: A machined diffusion plate D5321113910229 is installed under each frame foot between stations C24 and C31, spreading the introduction of the floor beam reaction over three fastener rows rather than concentrating it at the inboard corner. The foot fitting D5321110873831 is replaced by a thicker item with a larger radius at the critical corner, and the shear tie D5321112601390 is renewed to suit. The intercostal D5321114583888 is added at the four stations where the beam pitch leaves the longest unsupported span. The attachment row is drilled and cold expanded to the standard practice, using interference fit fastener EN824462K5 with the sealing washer arrangement required at the pressure boundary, and the remaining positions take collars EN650523-18 and rivets AGS622474-67. Access is from the forward cargo compartment in zones 113 and 115 with the lining and the floor panels removed; the lock actuator at FIN 21VU is disturbed and reinstated. Detail is on drawings D53211127822 and D53211223501.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 47 kg per aircraft for the full eight stations, forward of the reference station, with a centre-of-gravity shift of approximately 0.06 per cent mean aerodynamic chord that will need a weight and balance amendment. No electrical effect. The diffusion plate is not interchangeable with the plain foot and the modified stations cannot be reverted. Once embodied, the repeat inspection at the modified stations can move to the general structural sampling programme, which is where the operator benefit sits. Structure repair, illustrated parts and the frame foot inspection task all require update, and any aircraft carrying a published repair at a modified station will need an assessment.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Provisional estimate is eleven days with the forward cargo compartment stripped, which fits inside a scheduled heavy check but not inside a C-check. No production cut-in is proposed because the affected build standard is no longer produced.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether a foot that has already been blended twice retains enough material for the diffusion plate footprint, whether the cold expanded row can be applied to a hole that has previously been reamed oversize, and whether the published forward frame repair scheme can coexist with the plate. It must also confirm that the cargo lining attachment and the underfloor harness route survive the added plate thickness.

type_data.balance_impact: Forward of reference station, CG shift approximately 0.06 % MAC
